commands.author: clawsweeper[bot]
commands.review_summary:
The PR propagates cancellation to Gmail-search and GitHub-monitor subprocesses, preserves an in-flight Gmail send result, and halts later stages of direct tool pipelines after abort.

Reproducibility: yes. from source: resume an approval-backed pipeline with a completed side-effecting stage followed by the newly abortable Gmail search, abort during that search, then retry the old token. The provided review discussion ties this path to the new abort behavior, although no local runtime execution was available in this review.
commands.review_followup: - [P2] A narrow mechanical repair can preserve the submitted cancellation behavior while consuming prior resume state on resumed aborts.

target.title: fix(runtime): cancelled workflows no longer continue external commands
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where canceling an embedded tool pipeline could allow external work to continue or begin after cancellation. In particular, canceling while a Gmail send was already in flight allowed that send to finish, but the pipeline could then start a later side-effecting stage.

## Why This Change Was Made

Process-backed read operations (`gog.gmail.search` and the legacy GitHub PR monitor) now receive the parent abort signal, wait for definitive child-process termination, and use a bounded force-kill fallback when termination is ignored. Gmail sends use a narrower safety boundary: an already-started send is allowed to finish and return its definitive result, while direct pipeline-string tool requests preserve that output and halt before invoking another pipeline stage after cancellation.

The stage-boundary behavior is opt-in for the direct pipeline-string paths in `runToolRequest` and `resumeToolRequest`; workflow-file and CLI callers retain their existing halt semantics. Resume-state persistence, configuration, dependencies, and public schemas remain unchanged. Earlier review comments on experimental lazy-iterator and resume-state changes are no longer applicable because those changes were reverted and are not part of the submitted diff.

## User Impact

Canceled embedded tool pipelines now stop before later external commands can start. Abortable search and monitor subprocesses terminate promptly, a canceled Gmail search cannot hand off to a downstream side effect, and a Gmail send already in progress completes without an ambiguous result while all later drafts and tool-pipeline stages remain stopped.

## Evidence

The compiled production `runToolRequest` path was exercised with a real operating-system child process. Cancellation was injected after the first Gmail send process started in this pipeline:

```text
draft | gog.gmail.send | test.side-effect
```

Observed issue-specific runtime result:

```json
{
  "production_entry": "runToolRequest",
  "child_process_transport": "real operating-system child process",
  "cancellation_point": "after the first Gmail send child process started",
  "envelope_ok": true,
  "output": [{ "ok": true }],
  "completed_send_count": 1,
  "in_flight_send_completed": true,
  "in_flight_send_terminated": false,
  "downstream_started": false
}
```

The external `gog` executable was represented by a deterministic child-process fixture, so no Gmail account was accessed and no real email was sent. The production runtime, stage transition, abort signal, and operating-system process lifecycle were exercised directly.

Focused cancellation regressions:

```text
✔ parent cancellation terminates gog.gmail.search and skips gog.gmail.send
✔ cancellation after Gmail search completion stops the next pipeline stage
✔ cancellation during eager stage cleanup stops the next tool stage
✔ an in-flight gog.gmail.send completes and halts the pipeline after cancellation
✔ parent cancellation terminates the default github.pr.monitor subprocess
ℹ tests 5
ℹ pass 5
ℹ fail 0
```

Additional validation:

- `pnpm test` — 314 tests passed.
- `pnpm typecheck` — passed.
- `pnpm lint` — formatting passed; lint completed with four pre-existing warnings outside this diff.
